# infrawrench_resource_report (Resource)

A saved resource report: a table of synced resources across every connected account, with the columns you pick and the cost of each resource.

Columns are column ids. `core:name`, `core:type`, `core:provider`, `core:account`, `core:region`, `core:status`, `core:created` and `core:external_id` are on every resource; `field:<key>` is a key of the resource's synced fields; `tag:<key>` is a provider tag; `vtag:<key>` is a virtual tag, read from the resource's own cost rows over the cost range; and `cost:range`, `cost:mtd` and `cost:previous_month` are spend joined by the provider's resource id. The app's column picker shows the field and tag keys your resources actually carry.

Filters are AND-ed; an omitted filter does not narrow the report. The report is filed in the folder tree cost reports use, and shared with `infrawrench_object_sharing` (`object_type = "resource_report"`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "infrawrench_cost_report_folder" "platform" {
  name = "Platform"
}

# Every production EC2 instance and RDS database, most expensive first, with
# the owning team and last month's spend beside this month's.
resource "infrawrench_resource_report" "prod_compute" {
  name      = "Production compute by cost"
  folder_id = infrawrench_cost_report_folder.platform.id

  columns = [
    "core:name",
    "core:type",
    "core:account",
    "core:region",
    "field:instanceType",
    "tag:team",
    "cost:mtd",
    "cost:previous_month",
  ]
  sort_column    = "cost:mtd"
  sort_direction = "desc"

  plugin_ids = ["aws"]

  resource_type {
    plugin_id        = "aws"
    resource_type_id = "ec2-instance"
  }
  resource_type {
    plugin_id        = "aws"
    resource_type_id = "rds-instance"
  }

  tag_filter {
    source = "tag"
    key    = "env"
    op     = "in"
    values = ["prod", "production"]
  }
}

# Untagged resources created this year, for a tagging clean-up.
resource "infrawrench_resource_report" "untagged" {
  name         = "Untagged since January"
  columns      = ["core:name", "core:provider", "core:account", "core:created", "cost:range"]
  created_from = "2026-01-01"

  cost_range_preset = "90d"

  tag_filter {
    source = "tag"
    key    = "team"
    op     = "missing"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `columns` (List of String) Shown columns, in display order: 1–40 column ids (see the resource description). The first column links to the resource in the app.
- `name` (String) Display name, 1–120 characters.

### Optional

- `account_ids` (Set of String) Connected account ids to include (see the `infrawrench_accounts` data source). At most 200. Omitted or empty does not filter.
- `cost_basis` (String) `cash` for invoiced spend, `amortized` to spread commitment fees across the term they cover, or `blended` to also share each commitment's discount evenly across all the usage it could cover, so every team or customer pays the same effective rate (day totals match amortized). Defaults to `cash`.
- `cost_range_from` (String) A fixed window instead of a preset: inclusive start day, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Set together with `cost_range_to`, and not with `cost_range_preset`.
- `cost_range_preset` (String) The window `cost:range` covers and virtual tag values are read over, as a rolling preset: one of `7d`, `30d`, `90d`, `mtd`, `last_month`, `qtd`, `ytd`, `6m`, `12m`. Omitted (with no `cost_range_from`) is `30d`. Month to date and the previous month are always calendar months.
- `cost_range_to` (String) Inclusive end day of a fixed window, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `created_from` (String) Keep resources created on or after this UTC day, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Created is the provider's creation time when the resource reports one, otherwise when Infrawrench first synced it.
- `created_to` (String) Keep resources created on or before this UTC day, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `description` (String) Free text shown under the report name. At most 2000 characters.
- `folder_id` (String) Id of the `infrawrench_cost_report_folder` the report is filed in. Clearing it moves the report back to the top level.
- `name_contains` (String) Keep resources whose name contains this text, ignoring case. At most 200 characters.
- `page_size` (Number) Rows per page in the app, 1–500. Defaults to `50`.
- `plugin_ids` (Set of String) Providers (plugin ids, e.g. `aws`) to include. At most 200. Omitted or empty does not filter.
- `regions` (Set of String) Regions to include, matched exactly as synced. At most 200. Omitted or empty does not filter.
- `resource_type` (Block List) A resource type to include, with its plugin since type ids repeat across plugins. At most 200. None does not filter. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--resource_type))
- `sort_column` (String) Column id to sort by; it need not be a shown column. Omitted sorts by name.
- `sort_direction` (String) `asc` or `desc`, with `sort_column`. Omitted is `asc`.
- `statuses` (Set of String) Statuses to include, matched ignoring case. At most 200. Omitted or empty does not filter.
- `tag_filter` (Block List) A tag condition. At most 10, AND-ed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tag_filter))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned report id. Use it with `terraform import`.

<a id="nestedblock--resource_type"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_type`

Required:

- `plugin_id` (String) The plugin, e.g. `aws`.
- `resource_type_id` (String) The type within it, e.g. `ec2-instance`.


<a id="nestedblock--tag_filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tag_filter`

Required:

- `key` (String) The tag key, 1–256 characters.
- `op` (String) One of `in`, `not_in`, `exists`, `missing`. `in` and `not_in` need `values`; `exists` and `missing` take none.
- `source` (String) `tag` for a provider tag on the resource, `virtual_tag` for a virtual tag read from its cost rows.

Optional:

- `values` (List of String) Values to match, at most 200.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the report in the app, and in the
# --json output of `infrawrench resource-reports`.
terraform import infrawrench_resource_report.example 3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c9d-8e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f
```
